items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: Now this is our Naval Pre-Flight band. Benny Sexton played guitar, an excellent guitarist

ctx.x: Oh yeah. We were all thinking that. Everybody was thinking out there in the mud in the trenches. We were all thinking that. And also this was a chance, I was pretty raw, very raw as a musician. I had only been in the local, I joined in ’37 so I’d been in the local five years, and my experience — I was kind of limited. I had done little dance jobs playing with small groups. But we’ll probably get around to that as we go through my musical history. So I jumped at the chance. And it was a Godsend because in that…

lead alto players in the country. His brother, Ernie Royal, outstanding trumpet player who ended up in New York doing studio work, but they all were with the original Lionel Hampton band, the band that made “Flying Home.” Vernon Alley of course, Mister Music, he was in the band, Wilbert Baranco, who is mentioned in the Leonard Feather, who was a very fine musician/pianist/singer and arranger. Wilbert, during the WPA days, he had been connected with the music project in San Francisco, and he wrote for everything,…

three years at St. Mary’s College. See we went in, when they called us we were all put on temporary leave when they first recruited us. Then when they told us okay it’s time, then we got on the train and this was in 1945 [sic] around October, maybe the first of October, yeah, got on the train, the Western Pacific, and took off for Chicago.
